clue.text: I'm lucky to hit this card, having backed high

parts.note: a jack is a court card in a pack of playing cards

indicators.note: backed means the word for high is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: high as in uppermost, the top

explanation.surface: A gambler hopes to draw a high card, having placed a bet on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the word for high. 'I'm lucky to hit this' is the gambler's boast: the definition is a whole phrase, not one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambler who hits the biggest prize, the accumulated pool of a lottery or machine, is lucky indeed.

clue.text: Judge hopes to reform dreamer

indicators.note: to reform means the letters of hopes are reshaped

explanation.surface: A judge hopes to rehabilitate an idle dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical son of Jacob interpreted dreams and had them himself.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this son of Jacob is mocked by his brothers as the dreamer for his prophetic visions.

clue.text: Sort of bun is different, dunked into tea

indicators.note: dunked into means the word for different is placed inside the word for tea

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
else means different or other

explanation.surface: A particular bun is different, being dipped into a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiral currant bun named after a London district is a sort of bun.

clue.text: Untidy hair put up over piece of material: our style

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is turned to read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a mop is a shaggy, untidy head of hair
a pad is a piece of soft material

explanation.surface: Messy hair is styled up over a bit of fabric in our fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairstyle swept high off the forehead, named for Madame de Pompadour, is a style.

clue.text: I decline to pick up rings

indicators.note: to pick up in a down clue means the word is lifted to read backwards

parts.note: rot means decline or decay

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to collect wedding rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pick up' turns ROT to TOR. 'decline' looks like refuse, but means decay.
explanation.definitionFit: A torus is a ring-shaped solid in geometry; the plural names several such rings.

clue.text: Banker receives a club

indicators.note: receives means the word for banker takes the letter in, around it

parts.note: a banker is one who lends money, a lender

explanation.surface: A bank manager is welcomed into a gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' looks like a river bank or a financier; here it is a lender. Leander Club is the famous rowing club at Henley-on-Thames, England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leander Club is a celebrated rowing club in Henley, so the name is an example of a club.

clue.text: Energy is needed to hold shape

indicators.note: to hold means the word for is wraps around the word for shape

parts.note: is as in exists, lives
lines give something its shape or outline

explanation.surface: Energy is required to keep something in shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' places the shape word inside the word for 'is'; 'needed' is only a joining word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vivacity and vigour are both a kind of energy, a spirited animation.

clue.text: Spotted what sounds trite, commonly

indicators.note: what sounds means the result is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: trite means hackneyed, and commonly means in a Cockney accent, which drops the opening aitch

explanation.surface: Someone noticed what seems a trite, common remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commonly' marks Cockney speech, where the H of HACKNEYED is dropped; 'what sounds' says that spoken word matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin marked with pimples is spotted, from the skin condition of adolescence.

clue.text: What makes boarders cold at night, the sweet little things?

definitions.text: What makes boarders cold at night
definitions.meaning: ice in a dormitory, read as two words, would chill boarding-school pupils
small furry rodents that hibernate, regarded as cute

explanation.surface: A question about what chills boarding pupils at night, cute creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as dorm plus ice, the word suggests a freezing dormitory; whole, it names small cute hibernating rodents.

clue.text: In advanced age, nervously turning traitor

indicators.note: turning means the run found there is read backwards
In means the letters lie within the words advanced age, nervously

explanation.surface: An elderly person, anxious, turns traitor late in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points to EDAGENER inside 'advancED AGE NERvously', and 'turning' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter who betrays a cause or side is a traitor.

clue.text: Worked hard to accept what's badly made using old technology

indicators.note: to accept means the participle takes the shuffled letters inside it

parts.note: worked hard means strove, past participle striven

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of made are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone toiled to put up with shoddy goods produced with outdated machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' shuffles MADE to EAMD, and 'to accept' splits the word for worked hard after its second letter to take it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinery powered by boilers and pistons belongs to the Victorian era, an old technology.

clue.text: Took a single position in society, away from king

indicators.note: away from means the letter for king is taken out of the word

parts.note: one's rank is one's position in society
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Someone took up a lone social station, leaving the monarch behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a single' is cricket: a batsman scores one run by running between the wickets once.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a batsman who scores a single run between the wickets has hurried once along the pitch.

clue.text: Sort of vote to go so mad in America

definitions.meaning: a vote cast by mail rather than at a polling station
US slang 'go ...' means to fly into a violent rage

explanation.surface: A kind of ballot that would drive an American crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: A mailed ballot is a kind of vote; in American slang, someone who goes berserk at work has gone this way.

clue.text: Class doing simple task that's put up on the wall

parts.note: CL is a standard abbreviation for class
adding up numbers is a simple arithmetic task

explanation.surface: A school class does an easy exercise involving pinning something on the wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Exterior panels of timber or stone are fixed onto a building's walls as a protective facing.

clue.text: Fatal ruin — one copes, somehow

indicators.note: somehow signals that the letters are rearranged in some fashion

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A fatal disaster, yet someone manages to cope.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deadly or gravely harmful, like a disease, is fatal in effect.

clue.text: Impossible to see where hat could be

definitions.meaning: too difficult to grasp, as in seeing what is meant
literally the place a hat sits, on top of the skull

explanation.surface: A hat perched where its wearer cannot see it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means beyond someone's understanding; literally it describes a spot higher than the crown, where headgear sits.

clue.text: Don't participate, nursing depression: do you want to speak?

indicators.note: nursing means the phrase for not taking part holds the word for depression

parts.note: to sit out is to not take part
a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone sitting out while depressed is urged to talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' looks like low mood but is a hollow, a PIT.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase urges a hesitant speaker to say what they mean, idiomatically.

clue.text: Lose temper and breathe hard, but it's not serious

parts.note: to flip is to lose one's temper
to pant is to breathe hard

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and huffs, but it is all an act.
explanation.definitionFit: A glib, dismissive remark lacking proper respect is not serious.

clue.text: By airline, masses transported here?

indicators.note: transported means the letters of airline and masses are carried into a new order

explanation.surface: Crowds of tourists fly into a destination on a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' shuffles AIRLINE and MASSES. The answer, 'The Most Serene', is the old title of the Republic of Venice, a city where crowds of tourists arrive by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional nickname of Venice, a magnet for mass tourism flown in by the planeload.

clue.text: Drunkard's in the vicinity, showing defiant expression

explanation.surface: A drunk is close by, shouting something defiant.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's retort ending an argument triumphantly is a classic defiant expression.

clue.text: Not so calm when earring is damaged

explanation.definitionFit: Someone more cross is less calm, the comparative of being cross.

clue.text: Big person secures large shoe

parts.note: a fatty is an informal word for a big person
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A big person fastens a large-sized shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat heelless woman's shoe is informally called by this name.

clue.text: Don't carry on with heartless cherub: charming!

parts.note: a putto is a chubby cherub figure in Renaissance art
charming means nice, pleasant

explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the middle T of PUTTO to leave PUTO. 'charming!' reads as sarcasm but simply means NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shelve or suspend a plan is to stop proceeding with it for now, the idiom of freezing something.

clue.text: Plane is to crash-land

explanation.surface: An aircraft is going to make a crash landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crash-land' looks like one verb, but the hyphen splits it: 'crash' is the anagram signal and 'land' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom is a country, a land.

clue.text: Caveman offers a bit of fish to girl

parts.note: a fin is part of a fish
gal is informal for girl

explanation.surface: A primitive cave-dweller offers a fish fragment to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caveman' is not a prehistoric man: Fingal's Cave on Staffa in Scotland is named after the legendary giant.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary Scottish hero gives his name to a famous sea cave, so he is whimsically a man of the cave.

clue.text: Announcing grand party, shout

indicators.note: Announcing means the word is said out loud

parts.note: a ball is a grand formal dance party

explanation.definitionFit: To cry or yell loudly is to shout.

clue.text: Creature, a domestic one almost

parts.note: a pet is a domestic animal

clue.text: For silver in large quantity, one's beginning to transmute lead

clue.text: Time is useful, having to get over a natural barrier

clue.text: Some bug has got round modern equipment that provides services
